text.p: Capital & Regional Properties Plc on Monday celebrated its 10th year as a public company with record profits and the acquisition of a seventh retail warehouse park.
And it expects to make further acquisitions in its quest to become one of the UK's leading retail property companies.
"We are certainly always trawling the market," chairman Martin Barber told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Disposals are in the pipeline to allow the group to "regenerate equity" and enable it to make further acquisitions.

Some 14.5 million stg worth of properties for disposal are already in the hands of solicitors, but Barber said: "There is a lot more that we've identified, hopefully it will be much higher than that by the year end".

It announced the purchase through its joint venture Capital and Lanhan Retail Parks Ltd -- 75 percent owned by Capital, the rest by Lanham Plc -- of the Blythswood retail park for 17.1 million stg from Blythswood Investments (Scotland) Ltd.
The 27 acre site, situated near Glasgow, Scotland, is its latest retail acquisition since a policy change in 1993 to focus primarily on shopping centres and retail warehouse parks.
Barber said that leases totalling 55,000 sq feet had already been signed up for the site in between the negotiations starting and the acquisition being completed.
With Blythswood the company's gearing is now 118 percent -- "approaching the maximum level we feel comfortable with," said Barber.
While not ruling out further acquisitions before making any more disposals, Barber said he would like to see "one of the sales going through before we make those commitments".

Barber said he was comfortable with the level of gearing as the company's main control was the income to interest level, and interest is covered by just under two to one by rental income. "And that's what makes us feel comfortable," he added.
The company is likely to see the retail side of it business portfolio continue to grow. At the end of 1992 its retail share was "virtually zero". It now stands at 77.4 percent.

"This is a major strategic move which has taken place over the last three and a half years," said Barber. The company would continue to focus on the retail side over the next three years. "It wouldn't surprise me to see us in the 90s".

Industrials now only accounts for 7.7 percent of its portfolio and the office sector 14.1 percent. While unlikely that it would involve itself much further in the office sector, Barber did not preclude acquisitions in the industrial sector.
Barber said Capital & Regional had made "very significant moves" in its stated aim of becoming one of the UK's leading retail property companies.

He said the portfolio value of the group increased by around 6.3 percent last year. "I think what you're seeing is the tip of the iceberg as to what can be done with the assets we own," he said, adding that results from its investments will increasingly be evident over the next two or three years.

Capital and Regional earlier announced record pre-tax profits of 6.1 million stg for the year to December 25 against 4.7 million the year before. Net assets per share climbed to 229.6 pence from 186.5 pence
Earnings per share rose to 12.21 pence from 8.85 pence and the total dividend to 3.0 pence a share from 2.5 pence.
